The second-biggest prize left on "Monopoly 200X" is $50,000, with six of them remaining.

If "Monopoly 200X" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
696.headline: Where the prize money is

762.body:
The top prize count on "Billion" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has two of four top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

For "Billion" or any game, being late in a run is not automatically good or bad. The same numbers mean different things near the end of a run.

Everything here about "Billion" comes from official Ohio lottery numbers, current through November 18.
762.headline: No top prize claimed lately

827.body:
50th Anniversary's prizes make it a game built around small prizes that are won often. Of the prize money still unclaimed, about two-thirds is in wins under $5,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

The numbers for "50th Anniversary" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
827.headline: How the prize money is divided

847.body:
The $500,000 top prize on "Bingo 50X" is no longer available because all four have been claimed. The biggest prize anyone can win today is $100,000. Use that amount when you decide.

Everything above about "Bingo 50X" comes from the Ohio Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
847.headline: Top prize already claimed

891.body:
"Cash Explosion 25X" has 83,155 prizes of $5 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $10,000 prize, with one left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Tomorrow's count on "Cash Explosion 25X" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
891.headline: What's actually left to win
